name: Medial meniscus — anterior horn
description: Smallest part of the medial meniscus: on sagittal images a small low-signal triangle, clearly smaller than the posterior horn, anchored by its root in front of the ACL footprint. The transverse ligament often joins it to the lateral anterior horn behind Hoffa's fat pad.
variants_pitfalls: Transverse ligament pseudotear: the cleft where the ligament meets the horn can mimic an oblique tear, more often laterally. Follow the round low-signal ligament into the horn on consecutive sagittal images or one axial image.

The root insertion varies (flat intercondylar area 59%, medial plateau downslope 24%, anterior tibial slope 15%, no firm bony insertion 3% in cadavers); call a root tear only with a fluid cleft, displacement or extrusion.

Pseudoradial tear on coronal images: a blunted tip where the meniscus curves through the plane was seen in 79% of knees in one series, with no radial tears at arthroscopy. Confirm on sagittal or axial images.
An anterior horn larger than the posterior horn, with a deficient posterior horn, is a flipped fragment (much commoner laterally).
Anomalous insertion into the ACL or notch (about 1–15%, small series) and the oblique meniscomeniscal ligament (about 1–4%) mimic a displaced fragment; both trace to intact menisci.
